$comment: THE PHOTOGRAPH LICENCE GATE. No verified licence, no production image. Each of the three facts must be answered with a VERBATIM QUOTE and the URL it came from, and checks.py asserts that quote appears in the archived snapshot of that page under provider-terms/. That is the point: an answer cannot be typed from memory, because the evidence has to exist in the repository beside it. Run scripts/images/verify_provider.py to fetch and archive the live terms; it cannot run in the sandbox, whose egress proxy blocks both providers — which is exactly why the gate exists rather than a recollection.
$schema_note: Each of self_host, attribution, download_ping is {value, quote, source}. value: self_host true/false, attribution a string, download_ping true/false. quote: copied verbatim from the page. source: the URL. UNANSWERED anywhere means STOP.

self_host.question: May the file be downloaded and served from europedoor.com? This site sends `img-src 'self' data:` and checks.py refuses any third-party origin, so a provider that requires hotlinking cannot be used without an owner decision that changes both.
self_host.quote: All photos and videos on Pexels can be downloaded and used for free.

attribution.value: A prominent link to Pexels on any page showing a Pexels photo, and the photographer credited as “Photo by <name> on Pexels” linking to that photo’s page on Pexels.
attribution.question: The EXACT credit the terms require. picture() prints `<photographer> · <licence>`. If a link to the provider or to the photographer's profile or specific wording is required, the renderer changes BEFORE the first fetch.
attribution.quote: Whenever you are doing an API request make sure to show a prominent link to Pexels. You can use a text link (e.g. "Photos provided by Pexels") or a link with our logo. Always credit our photographers when possible (e.g. "Photo by John Doe on Pexels" with a link to the photo page on Pexels).

download_ping.question: Does using an image require a request to a separate endpoint? If yes, set endpoint_download.
download_ping.quote: You may not copy or replicate core functionality of Pexels (including making Pexels content available as a wallpaper app). Do not abuse the API. By default, the API is rate-limited to 200 requests per hour and 20,000 requests per month.
download_ping.basis: The API documentation's Guidelines section is where Pexels states what a consumer must do per request, and it names two obligations — a prominent link and photographer credit — and no event endpoint. No endpoint in the documentation tracks a download: the photo endpoints are search, curated and photos/:id, and the Photo resource carries no download-tracking link. Compare Unsplash, whose documentation has a `Track a photo download` endpoint and says outright that you must call it.

automated_acquisition.question: May photographs be acquired by an automated process — a scheduled or dispatched job with no person at the keyboard — and then served from this origin? This is NOT implied by a permissive licence: an API can impose conditions the licence does not, and the delivery condition is the one that decides it.
automated_acquisition.quote: The Pexels API enables programmatic access to the full Pexels content library, including photos, videos.
automated_acquisition.basis: The API's stated purpose is programmatic access, and its Guidelines section — where Pexels states what a consumer must and must not do — names four things: a prominent link, photographer credit, no replicating Pexels' core functionality, and no abusing the rate limit. None is a delivery condition and none forbids automation. The limits are volume: "Do not abuse the API. By default, the API is rate-limited to 200 requests per hour and 20,000 requests per month." Compare Unsplash, whose equivalent section states a hotlinking requirement outright — same kind of document, same structure, one says it and one does not, which is what makes the omission meaningful rather than merely unobserved.

attribution_layers.$why: FOUR FACTS, BECAUSE THE FIELD ABOVE ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS AT ONCE. `attribution.value` reads like a licence obligation and quotes the API documentation's Guidelines. Both documents are real and they say different things, so a renderer reading one boolean was reading an answer to a question nobody had asked. Nothing above is deleted: this separates it. See tools/lib/attribution.py for how the editorial renderer consumes it.

license_attribution_required.question: Does the ORDINARY content licence require the photographer or the provider to be credited on a page showing the photo?
license_attribution_required.quote: Attribution is not required. Giving credit to the photographer or Pexels is not necessary but always appreciated.

api.used_evidence: Every row in data/images.json carries a `provider_photo_id` and an `images.pexels.com` original, both of which only the API returns; scripts/images/acquire.py requests api.pexels.com/v1 with an Authorization header from PEXELS_API_KEY. There is no manual-download path in this repository.
api.quote: Whenever you are doing an API request make sure to show a prominent link to Pexels. You can use a text link (e.g. “Photos provided by Pexels”) or a link with our logo. Always credit our photographers when possible (e.g. “Photo by John Doe on Pexels” with a link to the photo page on Pexels).
api.scope_question: Does *whenever you are doing an API request* bind the application MAKING the request, or any surface DISPLAYING what it fetched? EuropeDoor requests once, inside a workflow, where nothing is shown to anybody; a reader's browser never contacts Pexels, because the CSP is default-src 'none' with img-src 'self' data: and every file is served from this origin. The archived text does not settle it and a renderer is not the place to decide it. Allowed values: requesting_application, any_display_surface, unresolved.
api.limit_tier_question: Ordinary/default limits, or an approved higher or unlimited arrangement? The higher-limit route carries its own attribution condition. Nothing in this repository records an application for one, and an absence of evidence in a repository is not evidence of absence: this is an account fact held by the provider and the owner. It is `unknown` rather than `false` for that reason.
api.limit_tier_quote: Do not abuse the API. By default, the API is rate-limited to 200 requests per hour and 20,000 requests per month. You may contact us to request a higher limit, but please include examples, or be prepared to give a demo, that clearly shows your use of the API with attribution. If you meet our API terms, you can get unlimited requests for free.

unlimited_api_requirement.question: Does the higher/unlimited-limit route's own attribution condition bind this product?
unlimited_api_requirement.why: No. That condition attaches to an arrangement a developer APPLIES for and the provider grants — *you may contact us to request a higher limit … if you meet our API terms, you can get unlimited requests for free* — and the owner declares that no such application was made and no such arrangement exists. It is `false` rather than `unknown` for that reason, and it does not make `limit_tier` `default`: the tier is the provider's record of an account, and the requirement is a condition on a grant that was never sought. Two facts, two fields, which is the whole argument of this block.
unlimited_api_requirement.evidence: The owner, asked directly, states no higher or unlimited Pexels API arrangement has been applied for or granted. This is not an archived page and is not recorded as one.

photographer_credit.question: Separately from the prominent Pexels link, what does the guideline ask about naming the PHOTOGRAPHER?
photographer_credit.why: The ordinary licence says crediting the photographer is *not necessary but always appreciated*; the API guideline says *always credit our photographers WHEN POSSIBLE*. Neither is an unconditional obligation, and the second is a softer wording than the prominent-link sentence it sits beside in the same paragraph. Recorded as its own fact because a renderer reading the prominent-link answer was answering this question too, and they are not the same question.

internal_provenance_required.question: Must the register hold photographer, source, licence, hash and dates regardless of what a page shows?
internal_provenance_required.why: This one is EuropeDoor's own rule and not the provider's: *no external licence claim enters production from memory; every externally governed asset requires source, date and evidence*. It is what makes `this file is the file that was licensed` checkable rather than a sentence, and it is unaffected by any decision about what a visitor sees.
internal_provenance_required.public_editorial_surface_why: The register's completeness is a rule about the REPOSITORY. It says nothing about whether a visitor is shown a photographer's name, and for a year it was read as though it did — which is how six editorial bands came to carry a roll-call. Provenance is published at /sources and in data/images.json; what an editorial page shows is decided by tools/lib/attribution.py from the two facts above and from nothing else.

unsplash.$warning: AN ASSISTANT'S RECOLLECTION ABOUT THIS PROVIDER IS NOT A FACT AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS ONE. There is a suspicion on record that the API guidelines require using the hotlinked URLs returned under photo.urls, require crediting both the photographer and Unsplash with links, and require triggering a download endpoint on use. Every one of those is a SUSPICION. It exists here only so somebody knows what to look for on the page, and it may not be copied into `value` without the quote that supports it.

self_host.question: Same question, and the one to read closely for this provider. Answer from the live guidelines, never from the warning above.
self_host.quote: Unsplash grants you an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide copyright license to download, copy, modify, distribute, perform, and use images from Unsplash for free, including for commercial purposes, without permission from or attributing the photographer or Unsplash.
self_host.basis: The licence grants downloading and distribution outright and attaches no hotlinking condition; the hotlinking requirement is an API-guidelines obligation and binds API uses. Its two exclusions are selling unaltered images and compiling Unsplash images to replicate a similar or competing service — this is a European travel atlas illustrating places it writes about, and is neither. So a photograph obtained from the website under the licence, without the API, may be served from this origin.

attribution.value: None required by the licence. EuropeDoor credits anyway: no image enters the register without a photographer, a source and a licence, so the credit exceeds the obligation rather than meeting it.
attribution.question: As above. If both the photographer and the provider must be credited with links, picture() needs a second link before anything ships.
attribution.quote: No permission needed (though attribution is appreciated!)

download_ping.question: If a download endpoint must be triggered on use, set endpoint_download and fetch.py will call it.
download_ping.quote: Unsplash grants you an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide copyright license to download, copy, modify, distribute, perform, and use images from Unsplash for free, including for commercial purposes, without permission from or attributing the photographer or Unsplash.
download_ping.basis: The download event is an API-guidelines obligation — "you must send a request to the download endpoint returned under the `photo.links.download_location` property" — and it binds API uses. The licence imposes no condition on use at all beyond its two exclusions. Under the licence route there is no endpoint to call and no `download_location` to call it with, because no API response is ever received. If the API route is ever opened, this flips to true and endpoint_download is already recorded.

api_route.question: May images be obtained through this provider's API? An API can impose conditions the licence does not, and scripts/images/acquire.py is an API client.
api_route.quote: All API uses must use the hotlinked image URLs returned by the API under the `photo.urls`  properties. This applies to all uses of the image and not just search results.
api_route.because: Fetching through the Unsplash API obliges us to embed their CDN URLs rather than serve the file from this origin. EuropeDoor sends `img-src 'self' data:` and a check refuses any third-party origin on any page, so that route would mean opening the Content-Security-Policy across all 1,033 pages to a host we do not control — an owner decision about the security posture of the whole site. The API route is refused and fetch.py enforces it. The LICENCE route is not refused: see self_host.

unread.https://unsplash.com/terms: Not yet read. The licence page links to it. It may impose conditions on any website user; nothing here relies on its contents.
unread.https://unsplash.com/api-terms: Not yet read. Governs the API route, which is refused, so nothing here relies on its contents.

automated_acquisition.question: May photographs be acquired by an automated process — a scheduled or dispatched job with no person at the keyboard — and then served from this origin? This is NOT implied by a permissive licence: an API can impose conditions the licence does not, and the delivery condition is the one that decides it.
automated_acquisition.quote: All API uses must use the hotlinked image URLs returned by the API under the `photo.urls`  properties. This applies to all uses of the image and not just search results.
automated_acquisition.basis: The architecture required here is acquire through the API and then self-host. This sentence forbids the second half for anything the API returns, and "all uses of the image and not just search results" closes the reading that it covers previews only. The two halves are not separable, so the answer is no rather than yes-with-conditions. A second clause points the same way and is recorded although the outcome does not turn on it: "The API is to be used for non-automated, high-quality, and authentic experiences." The article explaining that phrase is not archived and not read, which is why it is not the reason. Unsplash's LICENCE route — a photograph obtained without the API — is unaffected and is not this architecture.

license_attribution_required.question: As above.
license_attribution_required.quote: No permission needed (though attribution is appreciated!)

api.used_evidence: `api_route` is refused for this provider: the API guidelines require the hotlinked photo.urls and a download event, which would open img-src to a host this site does not control. No row in data/images.json names this provider.
api.scope_question: The guideline exists and this product does not take that route, so it binds nothing here. Recorded rather than omitted, because a requirement nobody wrote down is one the next person has to rediscover.

unlimited_api_requirement.why: The API route is refused for this provider, so no limit arrangement of any kind binds it.

photographer_credit.why: The licence says *no permission needed (though attribution is appreciated!)* and this product does not take the API route. EuropeDoor credits anyway in the register.
